ratings_why.fun: Voting toward the opponent you scouted is a real decision every turn, and the tiers ramp cleanly from one Vote to Mills paying the whole board; the stat growth itself is familiar per-trigger counting.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because it is the only tribe that changes both boards at once and turns scouting your next opponent into a turn-by-turn choice that judges every unit's Health shape.

verdict_why: Every tier does its job and the hot spots are bounded by caps or by Keeper dying; more passes would change it, not improve it.

points.text: Golden Gauge-Keeper fed tall, plus Tiddy Mun, can drown most of a board at Start of Combat with no answer but Health. Worth the owner's eye in sims; the cap in Risks is a ready dial.
Keeper of the Overflow lets Lower pay gold, stats and water at once, so Raise's own rewards look thin next to it. One more Raise-only payoff at Tier 4 or 5 would keep the choice live.
In turns 1 to 3 the water is usually 0 to 1, so Kees Kowk is often a plain 2/2. A tiny early Flood or a Level read would give the opener its job.
Say whether Kees Kowk's targeting beats an enemy Dive; a one-line rule settles it.
Master of the Nine Mills with Hendrika and Bram Stuw hits the nine-a-turn cap easily; the cap is the right brake, so keep it when tuning.

standouts.why: Stretch-Holder makes slot placement the High Water puzzle and is a clear weak point to hit.
Master of the Nine Mills pays either direction, so the Seesaw build grows big and stays bounded.
Board Almoner pulls against Stretch-Holder: you choose who stays low to be fed.

weakest.why: Kees Kowk has little to hit early, when Tier 1 most needs to win fights.
Ditch Coot's Flood 1 does little after the early turns.
Schouw-Walker is the only Raise-paid buffer and is a plain one.

flags.note: Golden Gauge-Keeper adds its full Health to the water; with Tiddy Mun that is a near board wipe late.
Overflow never resets; with Hendrika doubling Lowers it can grow very large in a long game.
Penningmeester with Sluiswacht and Hendrika pays six or more gold a turn, uncapped carry-over, for triple chains.
Kees Kowk targeting a Diving Under enemy: which rule wins is not written.
